title: Mock server exposes its admin API to the local network with a default password
description: npm run dev:mock listened on every interface with the admin password defaulting to 'dev', so anyone on the same network could use the mock dashboard API.
root_cause: server.listen(PORT) without a host binds 0.0.0.0, combined with a fixed default password.
intended_behavior: The development mock is reachable only from the developer's machine unless explicitly opted in.

conditions.description: Attacker on the same LAN while the developer runs the mock.

execution.attacker_perspective: Device on the same local network.
execution.observed_result: Mock admin API answers; it holds only mock data and in-memory keys that are never returned.

remediation.strategy: Bind to 127.0.0.1 by default; HOST env var opts in to other interfaces.

likelihood.reason: Requires a LAN attacker while the mock is running.

impact.reason: Mock data only; keys are never returned by the API.

confidence.reason: Node's default listen host is all interfaces.

title: Stored XSS through visitor questions in the dashboard log
description: Visitor-controlled questions and model answers are rendered in the Riwayat page.

trace.description: Log rows are built with innerHTML.

reason: Every visitor- and model-controlled field passes through esc() before insertion; markdown formatting in the playground runs after escaping.

title: Script injection through model output in the widget
description: Model output is rendered as a markdown subset in the visitor widget.
reason: Text is HTML-escaped before any formatting; only fixed tags are produced and links are not rendered.

title: Pages served without CSP or anti-framing headers
description: No CSP, X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors on the landing page or dashboard.
claimed_root_cause: No header policy for static assets.

trace.description: Static pages served without a header policy.

reason: Missing best practice without a demonstrated reachable exploit (no XSS sink found, dashboard actions need typed input). Added public/_headers as defence in depth.

title: Admin sign-in throttle does not stop password guessing
description: The admin middleware compares the bearer token with ADMIN_PASSWORD before consulting the failure limiter, and the limiter only runs on the wrong-password branch. Once an IP is 'locked', wrong guesses get 429 but a correct guess still gets 200, so an attacker can keep guessing at full speed and recognise the right password by the status code.
root_cause: The lockout decision is taken after, and only on the failure path of, the password comparison.
intended_behavior: While an IP (or the whole deployment) is over the failure budget, every admin request is refused before the password is evaluated.

trace.description: Any unauthenticated client reaches the admin middleware with an arbitrary Authorization header.
Token is compared with ADMIN_PASSWORD first.
allow('login-fail:ip', 8) is evaluated only when the comparison failed; a matching token skips it and next() grants full admin access.

conditions.description: Impact grows with a short or guessable ADMIN_PASSWORD; the owner chose a 9-character password.

execution.attacker_perspective: Unauthenticated client that can reach the Worker URL.
instructions: Run the Worker locally (wrangler dev --local) with a dummy ADMIN_PASSWORD.
Send 9 wrong guesses to GET /api/admin/status from one IP, then send the dummy password.
execution.observed_result: Before the fix: wrong guesses 9+ return 429 while the correct password still returns 200, so the throttle never limits guessing. After the fix (local run, dummy password): guesses 1-8 return 401, guess 9 returns 429, and the correct password during the lock also returns 429.

remediation.strategy: Check a durable lock (D1, per hashed IP and global, 10-minute windows) before comparing the password, record failures in D1, and compare SHA-256 digests in constant time.

code_changes.fixed_code: if (await loginLocked(c)) return 429; ... if (!(await secretEquals(token, ADMIN_PASSWORD))) { await recordLoginFailure(c); return 401; }

likelihood.reason: The admin URL is public and the chosen password is short and related to the product name.

impact.reason: A correct guess gives full dashboard control: replace the document, change the prompt and model chain, read the question log, and use stored provider keys.

confidence.reason: Source order is unambiguous and the fixed behaviour was reproduced on a local Worker with a dummy password.

title: Sign-in and per-minute limits live in per-isolate memory
description: Failure and per-minute counters were kept in a module-level Map, so their scope is one Worker isolate. Requests spread across isolates or data centres each get a fresh budget.
claimed_root_cause: Rate-limit state is not shared across isolates.

trace.description: const hits = new Map() holds all rate-limit counters.

evidence.description: const hits = new Map<string, { n: number; reset: number }>();

blockers: How many isolates and locations serve one attacker depends on Cloudflare's runtime placement, which is not observable from source.

validation_plan.local: Not reproducible with a single local isolate.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed: compare failure counts across rotating source locations against the Worker. The admin path now uses a durable D1 counter, so only the public per-minute limit still depends on isolate scope; the durable daily caps bound it.

title: Admin password used as the salt for visitor IP hashes
claimed_root_cause: Secret reused as a hash salt.

trace.description: Hash stored in the usage table.

reason: Only the owner can read D1, so no lower-trust principal can use the hashes to attack the password. Changed anyway to a random per-install salt as hardening.
